title: Aviation mechanic who may perform maintenance and approve return to service practice questions
description: Practice questions on who may perform maintenance and who may approve return to service under 14 CFR 43.1, 43.3, 43.5 and 43.7.

questions.question: A U.S. aircraft has only ever been issued an experimental airworthiness certificate. What does 43.1(b) say about Part 43 for this aircraft?

options.A: Part 43 applies to it in full
options.B: Part 43 does not apply to it
options.C: Part 43 applies only to major repairs on it
options.D: Part 43 applies only when it carries mail

questions.explanation: 43.1(b) says "This part does not apply to" any aircraft with an experimental airworthiness certificate, "unless the FAA has previously issued a different kind of airworthiness certificate for that aircraft."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.1, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 43.1(a), which foreign-registered civil aircraft are covered by Part 43?

options.A: Any that land at a U.S. airport
options.B: Any that are maintained at a U.S. repair station
options.C: Any that are flown by a U.S. pilot
options.D: Those used in common carriage or carriage of mail under the provisions of Part 121 or 135

questions.explanation: Part 43 covers "Foreign-registered civil aircraft used in common carriage or carriage of mail under the provisions of Part 121 or 135 of this chapter."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.1, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A light-sport category aircraft was not produced under an FAA approval. What does 43.1(d) say about the repair or alteration form specified in §§ 43.5(b) and 43.9(d) for it?

options.A: It is not required to be completed
options.B: It must be completed by an inspection authorization holder
options.C: It must be completed before each flight
options.D: It must be completed in triplicate

questions.explanation: Under 43.1(d)(1), "The repair or alteration form specified in §§ 43.5(b) and 43.9(d) is not required to be completed for products not produced under an FAA approval."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.1, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A shop helper holds no FAA certificate and wants to perform alterations under 43.3(d). Whose supervision does that paragraph accept?

options.A: A holder of a private pilot certificate who owns the aircraft
options.B: The aircraft owner, whatever certificates the owner holds
options.C: A holder of a mechanic or repairman certificate
options.D: A flight instructor who signs the helper's logbook

questions.explanation: 43.3(d) applies to "A person working under the supervision of a holder of a mechanic or repairman certificate", who "may perform the maintenance, preventive maintenance, and alterations that his supervisor is authorized to perform" when the supervision conditions are met.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.3, Persons authorized to perform maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alterations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A certificated mechanic lets an uncertificated helper do work the mechanic is authorized to perform. Under 43.3(d), how must the mechanic supervise that work?

options.A: By checking the finished work and signing for it at the end of the day
options.B: By being reachable by telephone while the helper works
options.C: By personally observing the work to the extent necessary to ensure it is being done properly, and being readily available, in person, for consultation
options.D: By giving the helper written instructions before the work starts

questions.explanation: 43.3(d) applies "if the supervisor personally observes the work being done to the extent necessary to ensure that it is being done properly and if the supervisor is readily available, in person, for consultation."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.3, Persons authorized to perform maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alterations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 43.3(a), on what basis may a person maintain, rebuild, alter, or perform preventive maintenance on an aircraft to which Part 43 applies?

options.A: Only as provided in 43.3 and § 43.17
options.B: Ownership of the aircraft
options.C: Possession of the manufacturer's maintenance manual
options.D: Employment by the FAA

questions.explanation: 43.3(a) states: "Except as provided in this section and § 43.17, no person may maintain, rebuild, alter, or perform preventive maintenance" on such an aircraft.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.3, Persons authorized to perform maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alterations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Pilots: preventive maintenance and part 135 approvals
questions.question: Under 43.3(h)(2), what must a pilot of a part 135 rotorcraft operator in a remote area have before performing an approved item of preventive maintenance?

options.A: A verbal go-ahead from the chief pilot for the day's flights
options.B: A certificated mechanic's countersignature on each item
options.C: A copy of the manufacturer's maintenance manual on board
options.D: Satisfactory completion of an approved training program and written authorization by the certificate holder for each item

questions.explanation: 43.3(h)(2) requires that "The pilot has satisfactorily completed an approved training program and is authorized in writing by the certificate holder for each item of preventive maintenance that the pilot is authorized to perform."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.3, Persons authorized to perform maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alterations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Pilots: preventive maintenance and part 135 approvals
questions.question: Under an approval issued to a part 135 certificate holder (43.3(i)), a pilot may remove and reinstall approved aircraft cabin seats. For what aircraft does 43.3(i) allow this?

options.A: An aircraft type-certificated for 10 to 19 passenger seats
options.B: An aircraft type-certificated for 9 or fewer passenger seats, excluding any pilot seat
options.C: An aircraft type-certificated for 20 to 30 passenger seats
options.D: An aircraft type-certificated for 31 or more passenger seats

questions.explanation: 43.3(i) applies to "a pilot of an aircraft type-certificated for 9 or fewer passenger seats, excluding any pilot seat," who may perform "the removal and reinstallation of approved aircraft cabin seats."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.3, Persons authorized to perform maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alterations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Pilots: preventive maintenance and part 135 approvals
questions.question: Under an approval for a part 135 rotorcraft operator in a remote area (43.3(h)), which condition must be met before a pilot performs the preventive maintenance items?

options.A: There is no certificated mechanic available to perform preventive maintenance
options.B: The pilot also holds a repairman certificate
options.C: The pilot holds an inspection authorization
options.D: The work is reported to the FAA by telephone

questions.explanation: One of the 43.3(h) conditions is that "There is no certificated mechanic available to perform preventive maintenance."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.3, Persons authorized to perform maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alterations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Pilots: preventive maintenance and part 135 approvals
questions.question: Under 43.3(h)(1), the preventive maintenance items a part 135 remote-area rotorcraft pilot is allowed to perform must be a result of what?

options.A: A scheduled inspection interval coming due
options.B: A passenger's request
options.C: A known or suspected mechanical difficulty or malfunction that occurred en route to or in a remote area
options.D: A manufacturer's change to the flight manual

questions.explanation: 43.3(h)(1) requires that "The items of preventive maintenance are a result of a known or suspected mechanical difficulty or malfunction that occurred en route to or in a remote area."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.3, Persons authorized to perform maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alterations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Pilots: preventive maintenance and part 135 approvals
questions.question: Under 43.3(i), when may an approved part 135 pilot remove and reinstall approved cabin-mounted medical oxygen bottles?

options.A: When a mechanic is on site
options.B: When the aircraft has been on the ground for less than one hour
options.C: When the bottles are empty
options.D: When no tools are required

questions.explanation: The pilot may remove and reinstall seats, stretchers, "and when no tools are required, approved cabin-mounted medical oxygen bottles."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.3, Persons authorized to perform maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alterations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 43.3(k), for a database update in installed avionics to be not considered maintenance, from where must the upload be initiated?

options.A: From a repair station's workbench
options.B: From the flight deck
options.C: From the avionics bay with the unit removed
options.D: From the manufacturer's ground station

questions.explanation: 43.3(k)(1) requires that the database upload is "Initiated from the flight deck," "Performed without disassembling the avionics unit," and "Performed without the use of tools and/or special equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.3, Persons authorized to perform maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alterations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 43.7(d), a manufacturer approves for return to service an engine it worked on under § 43.3(j). Except for minor alterations, in accordance with what must the work have been done?

options.A: Technical data approved by the Administrator
options.B: The owner's written instructions
options.C: Practices the manufacturer's mechanics choose
options.D: Any data a repair station supplies

questions.explanation: 43.7(d) says that "except for minor alterations, the work must have been done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.7, Persons authorized to approve aircraft, airframes, aircraft engines, propellers, appliances, or component parts for return to service after maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 43.3(j)(3), on which aircraft may a manufacturer perform any inspection required by part 91 or part 125?

options.A: Any aircraft of any make
options.B: Any aircraft it has repaired
options.C: Aircraft it manufactured under a type certificate, or currently manufactures under a production certificate
options.D: Aircraft owned by its employees

questions.explanation: A manufacturer may "Perform any inspection required by part 91 or part 125 of this chapter on aircraft it manufactured under a type certificate, or currently manufactures under a production certificate."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.3, Persons authorized to perform maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alterations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A mechanic has finished a repair on an engine. Under 43.5(a), what must already have been done before anyone approves the engine for return to service?

options.A: The aircraft owner has signed the work order
options.B: The engine has been run for one hour of flight time
options.C: The local FAA office has been notified
options.D: The maintenance record entry required by § 43.9 or § 43.11, as appropriate, has been made

questions.explanation: No person may approve for return to service unless "The maintenance record entry required by § 43.9 or § 43.11, as appropriate, has been made."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.5, Approval for return to service after maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A repair changes the operating limitations in the approved aircraft flight manual. Under 43.5(c), what must be done before the aircraft is approved for return to service?

options.A: The pilot must be told of the change before the next flight
options.B: Those operating limitations must be appropriately revised and set forth as prescribed in § 91.9
options.C: The aircraft must be test flown for 5 hours
options.D: The airworthiness certificate must be reissued

questions.explanation: If a repair or alteration changes the operating limitations or flight data, "those operating limitations or flight data are appropriately revised and set forth as prescribed in § 91.9 of this chapter."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.5, Approval for return to service after maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Who may approve return to service
questions.question: 43.7(a) bars approval for return to service after maintenance except as provided in 43.7 and § 43.17. Besides the persons those sections authorize, whom does 43.7(a) allow to approve?

options.A: The Administrator
options.B: The aircraft owner
options.C: The pilot in command
options.D: The aircraft's insurer

questions.explanation: 43.7(a) states: "Except as provided in this section and § 43.17, no person, other than the Administrator, may approve" an aircraft or part "for return to service after it has undergone maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.7, Persons authorized to approve aircraft, airframes, aircraft engines, propellers, appliances, or component parts for return to service after maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Who may approve return to service
questions.question: A certificated repair station repairs a propeller. Under 43.7(c), as provided in which part may the repair station certificate holder approve the propeller for return to service?

options.A: Part 61
options.B: Part 91
options.C: Part 135
options.D: Part 145

questions.explanation: 43.7(c) says "The holder of a repair station certificate may approve an aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part for return to service as provided in Part 145 of this chapter."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.7, Persons authorized to approve aircraft, airframes, aircraft engines, propellers, appliances, or component parts for return to service after maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Who may approve return to service
questions.question: Under 43.7(g), which repairman certificate holder may approve a light-sport category aircraft for return to service, as provided in part 65?

options.A: Any repairman employed by a repair station
options.B: A repairman holding a powerplant rating
options.C: The holder of a repairman certificate (light-sport aircraft) with a maintenance rating
options.D: Any repairman who built the aircraft

questions.explanation: 43.7(g): "The holder of a repairman certificate (light-sport aircraft) with a maintenance rating may approve an aircraft issued a special airworthiness certificate in light-sport category for return to service."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.7, Persons authorized to approve aircraft, airframes, aircraft engines, propellers, appliances, or component parts for return to service after maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Who may approve return to service
questions.question: A sport pilot performs preventive maintenance under § 43.3(g) on a light-sport category aircraft. Under 43.7(h), which aircraft may that pilot approve for return to service?

options.A: Any aircraft the pilot has flown in the last year
options.B: An aircraft owned or operated by that pilot and issued a special airworthiness certificate in the light-sport category
options.C: Any aircraft with a standard airworthiness certificate
options.D: Any aircraft used under part 135

questions.explanation: 43.7(h) covers "an aircraft owned or operated by that pilot and issued a special airworthiness certificate in the light-sport category."
